title: Cravings
subtitle: When You Want Something (But Don’t Really Need It)
bodyHtml:
Hey human. Let’s talk about cravings.

You know when I sit by the kitchen, meowing dramatically, pretending I’m starving even though I just ate? Yeah… that’s cravings. It’s not real hunger. It’s wanting — not needing. Humans get cravings too:
  • - I’m bored… maybe a snack.
  • - I’m stressed… maybe just one more scroll…
  • - I’m tired… maybe some sugar to wake me up.

Cravings are tricky.
They come fast, they feel urgent, but they pass.

Every time you don’t give in, you tell your brain:

“I’m in charge, not the craving.”

You build resilience — like a mental muscle.
Each small “no thank you” makes the next one easier.

I know it’s hard. I get dramatic too.

But you don’t have to follow every urge.
You can choose comfort that actually helps:

  • - Rest.
  • - Water.
  • - Movement.
  • - A soft blanket.
  • - A quick walk.
  • - A stretch.

Your body deserves care, not just quick hits.
Your future self will purr in approval.
